subject.title: Memory compaction blocks main processing lane, causing unresponsive bot for 10+ minutes

question: Should memoryFlush and preflight/overflow compaction be isolated or preemptible relative to foreground session lanes, and which transcript-ordering guarantees must the new scheduler preserve?
rationale: Current main still runs the relevant work through session/main lanes; fixing it safely requires choosing between lane isolation, cancellation/preemption, or narrower timeout recovery semantics.

options.title: Isolate Compaction Work
options.body: Add a dedicated or preemptible compaction/memoryFlush lane so foreground user messages can progress while compaction preserves explicit transcript checkpoint rules.

options.title: Keep In-Band With Shorter Recovery
options.body: Preserve current strict ordering and invest only in shorter abort, watchdog, and user-visible recovery behavior, accepting that foreground messages still wait during active compaction.

options.title: Defer Lane Redesign
options.body: Leave this issue open as the canonical scheduler decision and land only narrower fixes such as tool-result truncation, cancellation, or diagnostics in related items.

recommendation.title: Isolate Compaction Work
recommendation.body: Add a dedicated or preemptible compaction/memoryFlush lane so foreground user messages can progress while compaction preserves explicit transcript checkpoint rules.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter appears in command-lane, auto-reply, and memoryFlush history, which makes him the strongest routing candidate for the scheduler/product decision.
